rationale: Ground truth is thin and process-flavored (a 'do not change this' on musa.inc.md/quickstart.md and a '@FayeSpica PTAL'/'LGTM' sign-off on the npu.inc.md block), so neither reviewer can score high recall, but Y comes closer: it explicitly verifies musa.inc.md and quickstart.md are byte-identical to merge-base (confirming the revert reviewers demanded) and gives the npu.inc.md install block the deepest scrutiny of any section, echoing why that block needed a domain-expert sign-off. X's musa.inc.md finding covers similar ground but only one of the four ground-truth items. On the candidates' own merits, Y is far more actionable — seven comments each with precise file:line anchors and concrete suggested diffs — versus X's two comments, both missing actual line numbers ('README.md:?'). Both sets of findings appear grounded in the diff/repo rather than fabricated, but Y's greater specificity and verification depth (grep evidence, cross-file checks, a concrete git ls-remote suggestion) edge out X on precision as well.
